The brief this card thread handed its isolated contract-review subagent for head `fa8cdc935ac8cb21b1e70d8b861871dba6647000` (posted beside the record, per `references/contract-review.md`). The record follows in the next comment.

## Contract review brief — PR #37115 @ `fa8cdc935ac8cb21b1e70d8b861871dba6647000` (card #36997)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md docs/adr/README.md` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36997: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37115: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `fa8cdc935ac8cb21b1e70d8b861871dba6647000`
  · the check-runs on `fa8cdc935ac8cb21b1e70d8b861871dba6647000`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md, docs/adr/README.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a369c954-319d-59ad-9503-d19982af33e9/scratchpad/pr-37115/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa8cdc935ac8cb21b1e70d8b861871dba6647000`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md, docs/adr/README.md + none
Security-touching: yes

Read for this record: card #36997 (body and its three comments: two triage posts and the claim), PR #37115 (body, the two-file list, the net diff `e1dee7ae..fa8cdc93`), the check-runs on the head, epic #36996, sibling #36999, cloud#4969 and cloud ADR-0119. Cited code was read in the tree at the head with `git show` and `git grep`; nothing was checked out, built or run. The security line's `yes` is meant: D3, D4 and D6 teach permission behaviour (reads as the caller, refusals, withheld fields, the advisory `focus`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The diff publishes nothing.** Two files under `docs/adr/`: the new record and the regenerated index. No schema, no code, no changeset, no anchor under `scripts/adr-anchors/`. Right: the card's acceptance asks exactly this, and the record's Status line says it.
- **Accept-sets the record declares for later PRs, none landed here.** A metadata kind `ai_context` with six keys (row 5); the tool name `get_record_context` on `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES` (row 5) and `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE` (with cloud's registration); `ActionType` member `ask_ai` (row 6); `SkillSchema.context` (row 8); a citation shape with no schema (row 10). Each is additive and each is tied to a reader in the PR that adds it. Right against ADR-0049 and epic ruling 4. `ToolExecutionContext.focus` is #36999's, restated and not added here. Right.
- **`docs/adr/README.md`.** One row for ADR-0160, records 160 to 161, numbers 155 to 156, Proposed 8 to 9, total 161. Internally consistent; the index gate is in `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- **Gate verdicts, from the check-runs on this head.** `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `TypeScript Type Check` and the other lint and type-check jobs: success. The UI, docs-build, E2E and opt-in jobs: skipped by the path filter. `Test Core (1/10)` was still in progress at my last read; no run on the head had failed. The diff holds no code, so no test outcome bears on the two reviewed files.
- **Citations.** Every `path#Symbol` I opened exists at the head and says what the record claims of it: `registerObjectTools` and its read guard (`isSystemObject`, `aiReadExposed`), `wireBridgeTools`, `registerDatasetTools`, `textResult`, `withheldFieldNames`, `WITHHELD_FIELDS_NOTE`, `judgeRelatedLists`, `judgeQueryExpand` and the #35145 header, `callData` and `checkApiExposure`, `enforceApiExposure`, `createStdioDataBridge` (it takes `datasetTools` from the host), `serveReferenceNames`, `aiReadExposureRefusal` (the header's "would change nothing"), `CAPABILITIES_AI_WRITE_ARM_GUIDANCE` (the five spellings), `getDatasetToolJsonSchemas`, `createDatasetTools`, `createKnowledgeTools` (JSON Schema kept in the service), `resolveMcpDatasetToolsService`, `resolveMcpKnowledgeToolsService`, `routeToolCallsThrough` and `McpToolCallContext`, `ActionType` (the six members), `TARGET_REQUIRED_TYPES` (every type but `script`), `ActionAiSchema`, `isHeadlessInvokableAction`, `ActionRunner` and `RunnableActionType`, `SkillSchema` (strict), `skillPromptResult` (one message, no arguments), `skillBindingServed`, `useAiSurfaceEnabled`, `ToolExecutionContext` (no `focus`; the `surfaceContext` docblock's words), `pickSentenceLocale` (used by `service-analytics` and `packages/mcp`), `MCP_DOOR_TOOL_NAMES`, `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE`, `PLATFORM_TOOL_FAMILY_PREFIXES`, the `skill` registry row (the flags D1 copies), `packages/mcp/package.json` (no runtime dependency), AGENTS.md on the frozen `plugin-` prefix, ADR-0088's three clauses and its `validation` addendum, ADR-0005's ai row, ADR-0149 D2 and M1. `sys_user` declares `enable.aiReadable: true`, so the illustration's `owner` lookup is not refused by the system-object guard. "Nothing is taken" holds: the only other hit for `ai_context` is ADR-0149's mention of Cube's key of that name, which declares nothing.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff publishes nothing from any package, and `Check Changeset` is green on the head. `Clause-②: no` is right: no accept-set or published surface moves in this PR. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right for this PR; the record's split assigns `added` to rows 5, 6, 8 and 10, each in the PR that brings the key and its reader.

### ③ Boundary flags

The PR declares no `open_questions`. Its flags are the nine "Points that go past the card's words", the five corrections to the card's premises and the three "read first" items.

- **Point 1, pack selection.** Holds against the tree: `judgeRelatedLists` refuses "none, or several" with the candidates named, the same posture. The order of this refusal against the root object's gates is S1. Whether several packs on one object should refuse the `ask_ai` path is the maintainer's; the PR body escalates it and I add nothing.
- **Point 2, an object-level refusal is the whole call's.** Follows #35145 as the header of `mcp-relation-reads.ts` states it. What that refusal may name is S1. The choice between a refusal and a stated omission is the maintainer's; the PR body escalates it. cloud#4969 leaves "refuse or trim" to its PR, and D3 settles the open executor's side as refuse.
- **Point 3, no bare id for a lookup to an unreadable row.** Stricter than `get_record`, which serves the stored id. Safe. N2 on the dangling case.
- **Point 4, `anchor` on the same tool.** Holds.
- **Point 5, `related` one level, `body` an object.** Holds; it is the shape of `get_record`'s `related` less `orderBy` and `limit`, which D1 lists as later work.
- **Point 6, `ask_ai` takes no `target` and refuses `ai.exposed: true`.** Holds: `TARGET_REQUIRED_TYPES` excludes only `script` today and `isHeadlessInvokableAction` answers false for an unknown type. The spec already keeps `operation: 'update'` on the default `script` type, so no declarative-update route admits it.
- **Point 7, the MCP prompt names the tool call.** Holds, and it is what epic ruling 3 requires: the pack is a tool result, never prompt text.
- **Point 8, the read-set function is exported and the pre-read is a tool call.** Holds against cloud ADR-0119 D3 and epic row 9. N6 on the two computations.
- **Point 9, registry flags follow the `skill` row.** Holds: read at `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY`, the flags match.
- **The five corrections.** Each checked and right: the object-level key family; no shared wrapper (`textResult` serializes JSON only); ADR-0149 D2's two forms; a lookup to an unreadable target is left unexpanded, not refused (`judgeQueryExpand` judges the target by the read guard, which asks only the system-object question); `ai.exposed` is ADR-0011's.
- **D6 against #36999.** The contract line, the docblock, the name, the capability gate and the entry point match the card's items 1, 4 and 5 in substance. N3 on the one sentence left out.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The record introduces no id materialisation and no in-app join: the root is one `get`, a lookup is the engine's batched expansion, a related list is one capped query filtered by the parent link, and the body outline is text work on one field value. D3 binds every read to the read a record tool already makes.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md`**

What I tried to break and could not: no read leaves the caller's context (D3 forbids a system context and a driver read, and D4 seam 1 forbids a direct call of the render service); the related list is read as the caller, so no id, count or `truncated` flag reflects a row the caller cannot read; a root the caller cannot read answers as a missing one, as `get_record` does; a masked value passes through unchanged; a forged `focus` reads nothing, because the tool takes no `focus` and the record is named in the arguments; a skill's `context` or a `context` argument naming another audience's pack widens nothing, because the pack only selects among reads the caller's own permissions decide; every v1 key of `ai_context` and each of its sub-keys has a named reader in row 5; the six rulings are quoted verbatim from the epic; cloud ADR-0119 D1, D3 and D4 are summarised as that record states them, and D7's `ask_ai` and D8's prompt argument bring no in-product agent into the open edition; the implementation split's rows, lanes and blockers match the epic's table row for row.

Findings:

- M1 (must-fix) — **The "not visible to you" rule does not fire for an ordinary caller, and the record says the opposite in its TL;DR.** D3 "Field level" names a field as withheld only when the caller's served schema shows it and `getReadableFields` leaves it out; a field the served schema does not show "is omitted and nothing is said about it". Under ADR-0106 D1 a field the caller may not read is removed whole from that caller's served schema, D8 makes this the default, and D4 exempts only system and platform-admin callers. The tree pins it: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts` has "a member whose schema hides the denied field is never answered it" (withheld list empty) beside "an exempt author whose schema shows the denied field has it withheld". So for the epic's own scenario, an employee asking about a record with a field that field-level rules hide, the pack says nothing and the model has no way to tell hidden from absent. Epic ruling 2 reads "A field hidden from the caller reads 'not visible to you'", card item 3 reads the same, TL;DR item 3 of this record reads "A field hidden by field-level rules is named and reads 'not visible to you'", and the record states that no ruling is reopened. D3's body is the safe reading of ADR-0106, but it leaves the ruled sentence in force only for exempt callers or with the D8 switch off, and that settlement is not among the nine points handed to the approver. The tree holds a precedent the record does not weigh, in the very sentence of ADR-0149 D2 it cites for author defects: "a member whose fields this caller cannot read (step 4) is omitted for this caller, and the dataset entry carries `membersWithheld: true` ... the ADR-0090 D10 rule that a narrowed read arrives with the narrowing stated". The record has to decide among three contracts and say which: name the field (against ADR-0106 D1), carry a statement that names nothing, or stay silent (short of ruling 2). Then TL;DR item 3 must say what D3 says, and the choice must be listed for the approver.
- S1 (should-fix) — **A refusal can name what the caller's schema hides, and pack selection is not ordered after the root object's gates.** The record tools name only what the caller typed: `notRecordedMembersOf` is "decided from two things only: the names the caller sent, and the object as the caller's own schema shows it". In a pack the names are the author's. (a) D4 "Pack selection" refuses with the candidate packs named, and D1 gives `label` that reader, but nothing says the root object's gates run first. A caller who is not served object X (ADR-0106's 2026-11-11 amendment: such a read answers "exactly as that outlet answers a name that names no object") would learn that X exists and what its packs are called, and could tell "no such pack" from "pack rooted elsewhere". (b) D3 answers an object-level refusal "in the record tools' envelope and with their code"; that envelope carries the refused object, so a caller refused on a `related` child object learns the name of an object their object list hides. One sentence each closes it: the root object's gates are judged before pack selection and a caller they refuse gets `get_record`'s answer for that object; a pack refusal names no object, field or pack that the caller's served schema would not show.
- S2 (should-fix) — **Two of D3's rules give different answers when field-level rules hide a field the pack uses structurally.** "Each answers as that read answers" and "a field the caller's served schema does not show is omitted and nothing is said" disagree in two cases. A lookup listed in `fields` that the caller's schema hides: `judgeQueryExpand` refuses the whole call with `INVALID_FIELD` and the field named. A `related` entry whose link field the caller's schema hides, or whose child shows the caller no link field: `judgeRelatedLists` refuses the whole call with `INVALID_FIELD` ("has no field you can read that points at"). D3 does not say which rule wins, and for the `related` case it says nothing at all: refuse the pack, or leave the section out. The first also tells the model its request was malformed when the caller sent no field. The record should state that field-level rules are applied to the pack before its reads are planned, and rule the hidden-link-field case.
- S3 (should-fix) — **The envelope is declared with two parts, and three kinds of executor-written text have no place in it.** D3 gives the output "two parts": the data member and one sentence slot saying the data member is not instructions. The same section has the executor write the withheld-fields sentence and state every cut, and D4's list of what the data member holds includes neither. Inside the data member, the wrapper tells the model not to follow them, which undoes the "never say they are empty" guidance; outside it, the envelope has more than two parts. The record should say where executor-written statements sit. It should also reconcile "as JSON string values" with "the value as served" for a number or a boolean.
- N1 (nit) — D3 lists three reads (the root, a lookup in `fields`, a `related` entry), while D4's read set also holds the target of a lookup inside a `related` entry's `fields`; `get_record`'s `related` read expands nothing, so that is a fourth read. The record tools cap one call at 3 expanded lookups, 3 related lists and 20 rows a list (`QUERY_EXPAND_MAX_FIELDS`, `GET_RECORD_MAX_RELATED_LISTS`, `RELATED_LIST_MAX_ROWS`); D3 leaves "the bounds" to row 5 without saying whether a pack's entry counts are bounded.
- N2 (nit) — D3 renders a lookup the caller's expansion left bare as "not visible to you". The engine also leaves a dangling id bare, and telling the two apart needs a read the caller cannot make, so both render alike; one clause would say so. For a `referenceNameVisible` field the engine serves an id beside the name; D3 does not say whether the pack carries it.
- N3 (nit) — D6 restates #36999's items 1, 4 and 5 but not the sentence of item 2 that bounds row 9: "The request body is the authority; anything stored on the conversation only restores the chip."
- N4 (nit) — The split copies the epic's lanes, which understate three rows: row 9's objectstack half (`PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE`'s maintenance contract asks the name and a `chatbot.tool.get_record_context` label in every locale pack) has no objectstack row; row 7's form is a spec file by the `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts` precedent; row 8's key is a spec key.
- N5 (nit) — D8: a skill with `context` is not required to bind `get_record_context` in `tools`, which a runtime that filters tools per skill needs for an `anchor` re-read. The prompt's record-id argument is client text spliced into a platform-written line; D3's own rule suggests refusing a value that is not an id.
- N6 (nit) — D4 seam 3: an interceptor and the executor each compute the read set, and a pack published between the two changes it. The data door still enforces every read, so this costs nothing; one clause would say the set an interceptor judges is the call's plan, not a guarantee across a publish. D3's "no id, count or marker" should also say that the ADR-0090 D10 narrowing statement the record tools carry beside a narrowed list (`diagnoseDelegation`) is kept.

**`docs/adr/README.md`**

Generated by `pnpm adr:index`; one row and the counts, consistent with the new file's title, Status and date. No finding.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-qmmhf6`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZSA7o5vcLjQjM1myV`
Independence: rendered by an isolated subagent of that session at the review tier. It did not draft the record under review, read the dispatch order or take the drafting side's conclusions; its inputs were the card, the PR, the head's check-runs, the tree at the head and the cited records.

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81bd066b6fdb8395dad11f4018207ac9600768ba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md, docs/adr/README.md + none
Security-touching: yes

Delta round on the record of `fa8cdc93`. Read for it: the delta `fa8cdc93..81bd066b` (one commit, `docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md` only), the whole record at the new head, card #36997 and its comments (unchanged since round one), PR #37115 (body, file list, its two comments: the round-one brief and record), the check-runs on the new head, and the code the delta newly cites, read at the new head with `git show` and `git grep`. Nothing was checked out, built or run. The security line's `yes` is meant: the delta rewrites the permission contract of D3 and D4.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta publishes nothing.** One file, 73 lines added and 32 removed, all prose in the ADR. The net diff against `e1dee7ae` is still the two files under `docs/adr/`.
- **`docs/adr/README.md` is untouched and still right.** The delta changes neither the record's title, its Status line nor its date, which are what the index row is generated from.
- **Accept-sets declared for later PRs.** Two additions to round one's list, both tied to a reader: the `ai_context` schema bounds a pack's entry counts and refuses an oversized pack at parse (row 5); a skill that declares `context` must bind `get_record_context` in `tools` or is refused at parse (row 8). Right: each is enforced by the parse that adds the key, and the second touches no existing skill because the key is new.
- **New citations, each read at the head.** `packages/spec/src/ai/dataset-tools.zod.ts#DatasetToolCatalogEntrySchema` carries `membersWithheld`, and its description holds the quoted words "so an answer can say a measure exists that this caller may not see". The docblock of `notRecordedMembersOf` holds both quoted sentences. `QUERY_EXPAND_MAX_FIELDS`, `GET_RECORD_MAX_RELATED_LISTS` and `RELATED_LIST_MAX_ROWS` are 3, 3 and 20, and `get_record`'s related read passes no `expand`. ADR-0106 D1 holds "still leaks existence"; its D8 and D4 say what the record says of them. `mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts` holds both test names. `diagnoseDelegation` is a member of `McpDataBridge`. `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts` and `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/` exist, and the maintenance contract in `platform-tool-names.ts` asks what the split's note says it asks. `PERMISSION_DENIED` is the code `judgeTarget` throws.
- **Gate verdicts on this head, as read.** Success: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, the three scoped lint jobs. Skipped: `Check Changeset` (the PR carries `skip-changeset`) and the UI, docs-build, E2E and opt-in jobs. Still in progress at my last read: `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/10)`. None had failed. The two lint jobs that hold the ADR gates had not concluded, so this record gives no verdict for them; the seat reads their conclusions before it adopts this record.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round one and still right: `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` for a diff that publishes nothing. The split still assigns `added` to the rows that bring a key.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Point 10, for the approver.** It is a reading of epic ruling 2 ("A field hidden from the caller reads 'not visible to you'") beside ADR-0106 D1, not something either text says by itself, and it needs the maintainer's acceptance. The record presents it as that. The Provenance section flags it directly under the quoted rulings. D3 states how the two are held together. Point 10 names the choice and both alternatives not taken (name the field for every caller, against ADR-0106 D1; say nothing, short of ruling 2). The Consequences state the outcome in one line: an ordinary caller is told that something is hidden, never what. Two limits. The record hands all twelve points to "the approver" alike; it does not say that point 10, which construes a maintainer ruling, is the maintainer's own to accept. And the PR body was not moved with the head: its maintainer summary still counts nine points and still says a hidden field reads 「你看不到」 without the qualification, its D3 line still says "withheld fields named with the #35137 sentence", and its Verification names the old head. The PR body is outside the reviewed faces, so this is escalated to the seat, not graded: the maintainer's summary has to state point 10 before the maintainer is asked to merge.
- **Point 11.** Holds as a field-level rule against the tree: `judgeQueryExpand` and `judgeRelatedLists` refuse a caller-typed name the served definition does not show with `INVALID_FIELD`, and the record gives the reason a pack must answer otherwise. Its edge against point 2 is S4.
- **Point 12.** Holds: the root's gates before pack selection is the order `get_record` itself runs (`readGuard` first), one answer for an unknown pack and a pack rooted elsewhere removes the oracle, and one code for every object-level refusal of a pack-declared object is stated as a settlement.
- **Points 1 and 2** stay the maintainer's, as in round one. Point 2's alternative is now worded as the mechanism of point 10, which is accurate.
- **The declined half of N5.** The commit message declines a grammar check on the record id because record ids have no grammar to refuse against. Accepted: the id now rides as a JSON string value inside the arguments object and is never joined into the platform's line, which answers the concern.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The delta adds a fourth read kind, a lookup in a `related` entry's `fields`, as `query_records`' `expand` on the child: the engine's batched expansion, not a per-row read. Projection is metadata work on served definitions and reads no rows.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md`**

Round one's graded findings:

M1: closed
S1: closed
S2: closed
S3: closed

- M1. D3 "Field level" now has two branches and a statement that names nothing for the default branch, on the `membersWithheld` precedent; TL;DR item 3 says what D3 says; point 10 lists the choice with its alternatives. The statement depends on published metadata and the caller's served schema only, never on record data, and it fires nothing for an author defect, so it is one fixed bit and no oracle.
- S1. D4 "Order of judgement" puts the root object's gates before pack lookup and gives a refused caller `get_record`'s answer whether or not a pack exists. "The naming bound" limits every answer to the names the caller sent and what the caller is served, and gives one code to every object-level refusal of a pack-declared object.
- S2. D3 "The pack is projected before its reads are planned" fixes the precedence, and the third field-level bullet rules the hidden lookup, the hidden link field and the hidden body. D1 resolves a `related` link once on the published definition, so no caller follows a different link than the author declared.
- S3. The envelope has three parts. Executor statements sit in the notes, outside the data member the framing sentence covers; values are carried as served.
